statusDetail: Complete atomic audit of the sole unauthenticated archetype. Authenticated exchange routes were not covered because no credentials were supplied.

page.framework: ASP.NET-style server-rendered form with jQuery/Bootstrap-era frontend
page.notes: Root redirects to /Users/Login. Public navigation exposes only the login page; authenticated betting/exchange surfaces are outside this run.

paths.description: Root redirect and sole public login archetype; covers authentication entry, invalid required-field state, mobile/reflow, preferences, crawler/no-JS rendering, load/network/security, unknown-route recovery, and repeated input interaction. Authenticated exchange, account, betting, and transaction routes were not covered because credentials were not provided.

findings.summary: The login surface ignores dark and high-contrast preferences.
findings.evidence: Dark and prefers-contrast screenshots are pixel-identical to the default; the CSS probe found no color-scheme, prefers-color-scheme, forced-colors, or prefers-contrast rules.
findings.suggestedFix: Declare color-scheme and define preference-aware surface, text, border, and control colors with tested forced-colors fallbacks.

findings.summary: Transitions remain enabled when reduced motion is requested.
findings.evidence: Under prefers-reduced-motion: reduce, links and the Login button still report 0.4s transitions; no reduced-motion rule exists.
findings.suggestedFix: Disable or substantially shorten non-essential transitions inside @media (prefers-reduced-motion: reduce).

findings.summary: The component only adapts through viewport rules, not its container.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no container-type or @container rules, although the card currently fits at 360px.
findings.suggestedFix: Give the reusable login card a containment context and use container queries for internal spacing/type changes.

findings.summary: Keyboard focus is not visibly indicated.
findings.evidence: Programmatically focusing both inputs and both links produced outline-style none and no box-shadow; the button shadow is always present and is not a distinct focus indicator.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a high-contrast :focus-visible indicator with sufficient area and do not remove the browser outline without a replacement.

findings.summary: The only public flow is a password login with no visible recovery, registration, help, or cancellation path.
findings.evidence: The DOM and screenshot show only Username, Password, and Login. Both anchors have empty text; one points to #. No forgot-password or account-help action is visible.
findings.suggestedFix: Provide clearly labelled recovery/help and account onboarding routes, preserve context, and offer passkey sign-in where accounts support it.

findings.summary: Failure and recovery coverage is incomplete.
findings.evidence: Required fields rely only on browser validation with no live status region, while an unknown route returns Chrome’s generic HTTP 404 page with no site navigation or recovery action.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an accessible inline error summary/status region and a branded 404 state with retry, home, and support actions.

findings.summary: Cold-load LCP is slow in Lighthouse.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse measured LCP 5.2s and TTI 5.2s (performance 0.81). A separate trace measured LCP 1.12s, so the regression is variable but reproducible in the throttled Lighthouse condition.
findings.suggestedFix: Reduce the critical dependency chain and test under mobile throttling until LCP is consistently within 2.5s.

findings.summary: A tiny login page has an excessive render-blocking and font payload.
findings.evidence: HAR recorded 808,043 transferred bytes, 38 requests, 11 stylesheets, 15 scripts, ten parser-inserted VeryHigh-priority stylesheets, and 328,015 font bytes.
findings.suggestedFix: Inline or bundle only critical login CSS, subset/self-host WOFF2 fonts, and defer/remove non-critical libraries.

findings.summary: Duplicate and unrelated libraries are shipped on the login route.
findings.evidence: The DOM/HAR show two jQuery files, two Moment files, plus Select2, daterangepicker, countdowntime, Bootstrap, Popper, WURFL, and UA parser for a two-field form.
findings.suggestedFix: Build a route-specific bundle, remove duplicate jQuery/Moment and libraries unused by the login form, and prefer platform APIs.

findings.summary: Key controls and imagery lack accessible names.
findings.evidence: Lighthouse accessibility scored 0.80: the BP image has no alt and its 120px link plus a second href=# link have no discernible name. The form has no explicit visible labels beyond placeholders.
findings.suggestedFix: Add an appropriate logo alt/name, remove or name empty links, and provide persistent programmatic labels for username and password.

findings.summary: The page has no heading or main landmark and no visible focus treatment.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found zero headings and no main/nav/header landmark; focus probes found outline none on all focusable controls.
findings.suggestedFix: Add a descriptive h1 within main, retain a logical landmark structure, and implement visible :focus-visible styles.

findings.summary: The logo omits intrinsic dimensions and uses a legacy JPEG.
findings.evidence: The images primitive reports one image with no width/height, no alt, no srcset, and JPG format; the small observed CLS was 0.0016.
findings.suggestedFix: Add width and height, alt semantics, and serve an SVG or appropriately compressed AVIF/WebP where raster output is required.

findings.summary: robots.txt ultimately blocks all crawling.
findings.evidence: The fetched robots.txt contains a later `User-agent: *` and `Disallow: /`, overriding the earlier allow intent for general crawlers. The page itself has no robots meta block.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove the blanket wildcard disallow if this public login/brand surface is intended to appear in search, and verify with a robots tester.

findings.summary: The public login has no canonical indexing signal.
findings.evidence: DOM inspection found no rel=canonical. The root redirects to /Users/Login, making the preferred URL ambiguous to crawlers.
findings.suggestedFix: Choose the intended public URL and add a self-referencing canonical, keeping redirects and robots policy consistent.

findings.summary: The authentication page lacks baseline browser security controls.
findings.evidence: Headers evidence found no CSP, HSTS, X-Content-Type-Options, Referrer-Policy, or Permissions-Policy. The AntiForgery.WebExchange cookie is HttpOnly and SameSite=Strict but not Secure.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a nonce/hash-based CSP, HSTS, nosniff, Referrer-Policy and Permissions-Policy; mark all HTTPS cookies Secure.

findings.summary: The bare login route contacts unnecessary third parties.
findings.evidence: Tracker evidence recorded WURFL and Cloudflare Insights; HAR shows four third-party requests and 15,374 transferred bytes, while no known advertising tracker or exposed secret was found.
findings.suggestedFix: Remove device-detection/analytics calls from authentication until needed, or document and minimize their data collection.

findings.summary: Authentication is password-only with no phishing-resistant option.
findings.evidence: The only sign-in controls are username and password; source inspection found no WebAuthn/passkey affordance. No permission prompt occurred on load.
findings.suggestedFix: Offer WebAuthn/passkey authentication and account recovery alongside password fallback.

findings.summary: The document language is set, but the CSS is not writing-mode resilient.
findings.evidence: The page has html lang=en, but CSS inspection found no logical inline/block properties and no dir declaration.
findings.suggestedFix: Use logical properties for spacing/positioning and set/derive direction so translated RTL layouts remain usable.

findings.summary: Sign-in fields omit autocomplete tokens.
findings.evidence: The username and password inputs both expose an empty autocomplete value.
findings.suggestedFix: Use autocomplete=username and autocomplete=current-password, and add the corresponding WebAuthn token when passkeys are available.

findings.summary: The asset budget is disproportionate to the two-field page.
findings.evidence: HAR transferred 808KB, including 328KB of fonts and 50KB of images; the sole content image is JPEG without responsive sources, while numerous decorative/vendor assets load eagerly.
findings.suggestedFix: Set a small route budget, subset fonts, optimize the background/logo, and avoid loading unrelated component assets.

findings.summary: The interactive form has no transition treatment for state changes.
findings.evidence: CSS inspection found no view-transition declarations or API use; form state is swapped through conventional DOM/CSS behavior.
findings.suggestedFix: Use a same-document View Transition for meaningful login state changes such as pending, error, and recovery panels, while honoring reduced motion.

taskList.title: Harden the authentication response and cookie policies
Make login accessible with names, landmarks, and visible focus
Add recovery routes, passkeys, and correct sign-in autocomplete
Strip the login route to a small critical bundle
Respect theme, contrast, and reduced-motion preferences
Modernize and dimension the logo asset
Add progressive state transitions to the login flow
